stories.headline: Red Sox broadcaster rips Jazz Chisholm Jr. as 'bush league player'
stories.summary: The Red Sox radio play-by-play announcer ripped Jazz Chisholm Jr. during Sunday's game against the Yankees, calling the second baseman a "bush league player" and suggesting that Boston should "drill" one of his teammates.
stories.body:
The Boston Red Sox radio play-by-play announcer ripped New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. during Sunday's game between the longtime rivals, calling the two-time All-Star a "bush league player" and suggesting that Boston should "drill" one of his teammates.

Will Flemming, who calls games on Boston radio station WEEI, unloaded on Chisholm in the eighth inning of New York's 16-1 victory Sunday at Yankee Stadium.

With the Yankees holding a 7-1 lead, Chisholm drew a leadoff walk against Red Sox left-hander Jovani Moran and stole second base. Boston elected not to hold Chisholm on at second, so he also promptly stole third base without a throw, drawing the ire of Flemming and WEEI color analyst Will Middlebrooks.

"Chisholm's doing it again," Flemming said as Chisholm trotted into third. "This is what he does."

As Middlebrooks bemoaned Chisholm stealing extra bases while New York held a six-run lead, Flemming added that Moran should retaliate against Yankees catcher Austin Wells, who was batting at the time.

"Wouldn't you sort of like to see Moran drill Wells right here?" Flemming said.

Middlebrooks responded that Chisholm was being "selfish" and "padding your stats," while Flemming added that Chisholm "is a bush league player."

Three pitches later, Wells lined a two-run home run into right field to plate Chisholm, whose slow trot down the third base line drew another rebuke from Flemming.

"Moran should fight Chisholm," Flemming said. "[Moran] is walking toward the third base line, staring at him there."

Flemming said the situation likely added "a little extra vinegar" to a potential Red Sox-Yankees postseason series before again turning his attention to Chisholm.

"I'm gonna say it, he plays the game the wrong way," said Flemming, who also added that Chisholm is "awesome" and "so talented."

The Yankees ultimately rolled in what had been a tight game before a pivotal play in the fifth inning, when umpires ruled that Red Sox center fielder Ceddane Rafaela trapped Chisholm's low line drive, turning a possible inning-ending double play into a base hit that extended the inning. New York scored five runs in the inning en route to a crucial victory.

The Yankees (78-59) moved four games ahead of the Red Sox (74-63) for the American League's top wild card spot and also clinched the season series to win a tiebreaker should the rivals finish the regular season with the same record.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Spurs to make late move for Pulisic?
stories.summary: The deadline for the summer window in Europe closes tomorrow, and Tottenham Hotspur are interested in AC Milan winger Christian Pulisic. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
USMNT and AC Milan winger Christian Pulisic is of interest to Tottenham Hotspur, while AC Milan have Manchester United defender Leny Yoro and Barcelona left back Alejandro Balde. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Tottenham Hotspur are interested in AC Milan winger Christian Pulisic, according to TEAMtalk. It is reported that the Premier League side have made an inquiry for the 27-year-old, having identified him as a potential alternative signing to Liverpool winger and Manchester City-linked Cody Gakpo. Spurs are among multiple teams to have checked on the situation of USMNT star Pulisic, who played no part in the 2-0 Serie A win over Venezia on Friday as he continues his return from injury. Spurs are also working on a deal to sign center back Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea to replace Kevin Danso, says Fabrizio Romano.

- Chelsea have made AS Roma midfielder Manu Koné their priority target to replace Enzo Fernández, says Footmercato. Koné, 25, has been linked with a €40 million exit all summer, but if Argentina international Fernández completes a £120 million move to Manchester City before the window shuts, then the Blues will move for Koné.

- AC Milan have Manchester United defender Leny Yoro and Barcelona left back Alejandro Balde on their shortlist, Tuttosport reports. Yoro, 20 is reportedly among several players being considered by the Rossoneri, who are exploring the market for defenders, with plans to offload Fikayo Tomori and find a long term option at full back. It is reported that a move for 22-year-old Balde would require an offer worth around €50 million.

- Barcelona are monitoring the situation of Internazionale wing back Federico Dimarco, Gazzetta dello Sport reports. The Blaugrana see the 28-year-old as a key starter due to his ability in the attacking third, but aware of growing interest from the LaLiga club, the Nerazzurri are now considering talks to sign him to a new contract extension. Dimarco made 46 appearances across all competitions for Inter last season.

- Chelsea, Aston Villa, and Newcastle are looking at Bayer Leverkusen striker Christian Kofane, Football Insider reports. All three sides are reportedly exploring a swoop to sign the 20-year-old before the transfer window closes on Tuesday, with the Blues viewing him as a high-potential prospect for the future. Kofane began the new Bundesliga campaign with a goal when coming on as a substitute to score in the 3-2 defeat against SV Elversberg on Saturday.

ESPN sources
- Liverpool are closing in on a deal to sign goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans from Belgian side Genk. Liverpool look set to agree a deal in the region of €35 million, although it is likely the 18-year-old will remain on loan at Genk this season. Read

- Fiorentina are set to sign striker Beto from Everton for a fee in the region of £15 million. Beto, 28, is set to have his medical in Florence on Monday and his departure could prompt Everton to move for United States forward Folarin Balogun. Read

- Barcelona are in "very advanced" negotiations with Arsenal over a deal to sign Brazilian striker Gabriel Jesus. Jesus, 29, has just one year to run on his contract with the English champions and has emerged as an option for Barça following their failure to land Julián Álvarez. Read

- Women's Super League (WSL) side Manchester United are finalizing a deal to sign Mexico international Rebeca Bernal from the NWSL's Washington Spirit. According to the source, an announcement is expected at some point ahead of Manchester United's season-opener on Sept. 4. Read

Done deals

- City's women's side have signed Germany international right back Carlotta Wamser from Bayer Leverkusen. Read

- Nottingham Forest have signed full back Daniel Muñoz from Crystal Palace for a fee of £22 million.

- England international striker Ollie Watkins has joined Al Hilal from Aston Villa for around £51 million, the Saudi Pro League club announced. Read

stories.headline: A'ja Wilson, Kelsey Plum to miss the FIBA Women's World Cup
stories.summary: Kelsey Plum and A'Ja Wilson will miss the FIBA Women's World Cup for health reasons, with the Mercury announcing that Plum will miss the rest of the 2026 season. Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron will replace Plum and Wilson, USA Basketball announced Monday.
stories.body:
A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum will miss the FIBA Women's World Cup for health reasons with Plum also missing the rest of the 2026 WNBA season.

USA Basketball announced Monday that Washington teammates Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron would replace Wilson and Plum on the FIBA World Cup roster,

Wilson, the four-time WNBA MVP, has shouldered quite a workload in the first part of the season for the Las Vegas Aces and needed a break to rest and get ready for the playoffs. She was voted the most outstanding player of the 2024 Paris Olympics and the 2022 World Cup. She will be sorely missed by the United States.

Plum has been dealing with a calf injury for most of the WNBA season and it still hasn't 100% healed. She was a catalyst in the Paris Games gold-medal contest against France and sparked the Americans to the one-point victory.

In announcing the end of Plum's season, Mercury general manager Nick U'Ren said, "Kelsey is a competitor, and she wants nothing more than to be on the court with her teammates and competing for the Mercury. We know how much it means to her to play, and how much she means to our fans. Ultimately, this was about doing what is best for Kelsey's long-term health and making sure she has the time and support she needs to return to the court at full strength."

Iriafen and Citron were both part of U.S. camps this past winter. Iriafen played on the American team that went to Puerto Rico and won the World Cup qualifier. Citron had to miss that tournament because of an injury, so she'll be making her national team debut in Germany.

The Americans have won every World Cup since finishing with the bronze medal in 2006. That World Cup saw American star Lisa Leslie pull out at the last minute because of a car accident that her uncle was in. Without her, the U.S. fell to Russia in the semifinals.

Without the two veteran players, the U.S. will rely even more heavily on its youth movement. Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers will make their World Cup. The young stars will be joined by Olympic medalists Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, Chelsea Gray, Jackie Young and Kahleah Copper.

Rhyne Howard and Aliyah Boston will also be making their World Cup debuts to round out the team.

The U.S. opens against China on Friday. The Chinese team has a huge front line with 7-foot-3 Zhang Ziyu, 6-10 Han Xu and 6-7 Li Yueru. The two teams played for the World Cup title in 2022 in Australia.

Information from The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: NBA offseason recap, early 2026-27 season previews by team
stories.summary: We're looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the regular season by rolling out one team profile each weekday through Sept. 18.
stories.body:
After an eventful July full of big trades, intriguing signings and the game's biggest star shocking everyone by heading East, the NBA offseason is nearly complete. And with the regular-season schedule now out, it's time to start thinking about the 2026-27 season.

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Sept. 18. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for every team.

Check out the rollout schedule below, with stories added daily:

Quick links:

Free agency buzz | FA grades | Trade grades

Transactions | Schedule | More NBA coverage

Southeast Division

Miami Heat: Aug. 31
Key additions: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Klay Thompson, Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr., Nick Richards

Key retentions: Andrew Wiggins, Simone Fontecchio

Key subtractions: Tyler Herro, Norman Powell, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis

Heat president Pat Riley landed the superstar he'd been searching for since LeBron James left Miami in 2016. Antetokounmpo is in the fold, and Miami is ready to contend for another title with the two-time MVP. Antetokounmpo is just as motivated to win his second title and remind everyone that he can be the best player in the league.

In the trade, the Heat gave up key players such as Herro, Ware and Jaquez and did not bring back Powell in free agency. They landed Thompson to a two-year, $13 million deal after the four-time champion sharpshooter worked out a buyout with the Dallas Mavericks. Miami also added Portis and Hardaway, but the team is still looking to bolster the roster around Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo. -- Ohm Youngmisuk

Washington Wizards: Sept. 1

Charlotte Hornets: Sept. 2

Atlanta Hawks: Sept. 3

Pacific Division

Los Angeles Lakers: Aug. 24
Key additions: C Walker Kessler, F Sandro Mamukelashvili, G Quentin Grimes, G Collin Sexton, F Kevon Looney, F Matisse Thybulle, G Cameron Carr

Key retentions: G Austin Reaves

Key subtractions: F LeBron James, C Deandre Ayton, G Marcus Smart, F Rui Hachimura, G Luke Kennard, C Jaxson Hayes

James informed the Lakers he would not be returning for next season on June 30. Two days later, the team transformed the roster, with Doncic squarely as the focal point.

The biggest addition -- literally and figuratively -- is 7-foot-2 center Kessler, acquired in a sign-and-trade deal with the Utah Jazz. L.A. sent two unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and pick swaps in 2028 and 2030, not to mention a four-year, $130 million contract, to acquire him.

Mamukelashvili, Grimes, Sexton, Looney and Thybulle also signed with the Lakers, and free agent Ziaire Williams and first-round pick Carr bolster the team's young prospect pool of Adou Thiero, Bronny James and Dalton Knecht.

The most important move, though, came when Reaves, coming off a career season in which he averaged 23.3 points, 4.7 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game, signed a four-year, $180 million extension.

When the dust settled, it was a dramatic roster overhaul in what could prove to be one of the most consequential summers in franchise history, with the team also being sold for the second time in 14 months, this time to venture capitalist Josh Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger, who bought the Lakers from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Lakers offseason recap/season preview

LA Clippers: Aug. 25
Key additions: Rui Hachimura, Keaton Wagler, Brandon Ingram (TBD), Gradey Dick (TBD)

Key retentions: Kobe Sanders, Bradley Beal

Key subtractions: Kawhi Leonard (TBD), Nicolas Batum, Bogdan Bogdanovic, John Collins

What started as a reconfiguration at the trade deadline -- acquiring Darius Garland from Cleveland for James Harden and Bennedict Mathurin from Indiana for Ivica Zubac -- turned into a complete overhaul this summer after the Clippers let Bogdan Bogdanovic, Nicolas Batum and John Collins walk.

Their biggest move, however, was trading Leonard to the Toronto Raptors for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and draft picks, but that deal is in limbo pending the investigation into alleged salary cap circumvention by the team relating to Leonard's Aspiration endorsement deal.

In the meantime, LA added Illinois guard Wagler with the No. 5 pick in the draft and signed Hachimura away from the crosstown Lakers with a two-year, $28 million deal. And in a surprise move, Bradley Beal -- after declining his $5.6 million contract option for next season in June to test free agency -- ended up re-signing on a two-year, $13.2 million deal in mid-August to stay with the Clippers. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Clippers offseason recap/season preview

Golden State Warriors: Aug. 26
Key additions: Yaxel Lendeborg, Brandon Williams, Georges Niang

Key subtractions: Quinten Post, Pat Spencer

Key retentions: Draymond Green, Al Horford, Kristaps Porzingis, Gary Payton II, De'Anthony Melton

The Warriors opted for flexibility and stability over a larger shake-up around Curry. Their much-publicized recruitment of James never gained much traction.

They brought back their veteran frontcourt trio (Green, Horford, Porzingis), but kept them all on short-term maneuverable contracts. They opted for the fit of Melton over a pursuit of scoring guard Anfernee Simons. Their big addition is Lendeborg, the 23-year-old rookie wing who they will rely upon to be a high-minute, high-impact rotation player immediately.

In the bigger picture, they protected their draft pick cupboard and lined up their books to have an ocean of cap space as they peer a bit deeper into the future while their core ages. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Warriors offseason recap/season preview

Phoenix Suns: Aug. 27
Key additions: F Miles Bridges, F Koa Peat, G Luke Kennard

Key subtractions: G Grayson Allen, F Royce O'Neale

Key retentions: F Dillon Brooks, G Collin Gillespie, C Mark Williams, G Jordan Goodwin

Phoenix followed up its surprising season with a series of moves to mostly keep its team intact, with some adjustments around the margins.

The Suns re-signed Gillespie (four years, $48 million), Williams (three years, $38 million), Goodwin (three years, $19 million) and Brooks (three years, $73 million) to new deals and made a major splash by trading Allen and O'Neale to the Charlotte Hornets for Bridges. And despite not having a pick until No. 47 in the second round of the 2026 draft, Phoenix was able to acquire Arizona player Peat -- who averaged 14.1 points on 52.8% shooting as a freshman for the Wildcats and was key to their Final Four run. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Suns offseason recap/season preview

Sacramento Kings: Aug. 28
Key additions: G Darius Acuff Jr., F Alex Karaban, G Emanuel Sharp

Key subtractions: G DeMar DeRozan, G Russell Westbrook

Key retentions: F Precious Achiuwa

Perry, currently in the organization's power seat, is continuing a steady transition toward the younger core he has drafted. Arkansas guard and No. 7 pick Acuff is the spotlight name on a roster populated with six players in their first two NBA seasons.

But they still have notable high-minute holdovers from the past regime, including Murray, Malik Monk, LaVine and Sabonis. Of those four, Murray appears the most locked-in as a stable member of the team's long-term vision. Perry explored trades for Monk, LaVine and Sabonis over the past year, but didn't value the proposed returns, and the three are expected to open the season in Sacramento. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Kings offseason recap/season preview

Northwest Division

Portland Trail Blazers: Aug. 17
Key additions: G Ja Morant, F Jeremy Sochan

Key retentions: C Robert Williams III

Key subtractions: F Jerami Grant, F Kris Murray, G Matisse Thybulle

Sadly, the Blazers made far more noise this offseason with their off-court business dealings than anything they did with their roster. New owner Tom Dundon's aggressive cost-cutting measures and ongoing fight for arena financing have distracted from the progress that Portland made on the court last season, when it reached the playoffs for the first time since 2021.

Although the Blazers were the only team that sat out June's draft by not making a pick, they will add two high-profile guards to a rotation that otherwise looks very similar to last season. Lillard, a franchise icon, is back from an Achilles tendon injury that sidelined him for the entire 2025-26 campaign, and Morant, a two-time All-Star, arrived in a trade that sent Grant and Murray to the Memphis Grizzlies. -- Ben Golliver

Read the full Blazers offseason recap/season preview

Utah Jazz: Aug. 18
Key additions: G Darryn Peterson, C Jaxson Hayes, G Josh Okogie

Key retentions: C Jusuf Nurkic

Key subtractions: C Walker Kessler

The Jazz finally got some lottery luck, landing at No. 2 and taking Peterson, a gifted guard who has the potential to emerge as the face of the franchise. The hope was that Peterson would be the final major piece in Utah's rebuild, but that plan featured Kessler as the team's long-term starting center. Instead, the Jazz agreed to a sign-and-trade deal that sent Kessler to the Lakers in exchange for a pair of future first-round picks and two swaps.

The return was widely considered to be great value for Utah, particularly after Kessler's deal (four years, $130 million) pushed beyond the Jazz's comfort zone, but there is now a glaring need in the starting lineup alongside Jackson and Lauri Markkanen in the frontcourt. -- Tim MacMahon

Read the full Jazz offseason recap/season preview

Minnesota Timberwolves: Aug. 19
Key additions: G LaMelo Ball, G Josh Green, G Isaiah Evans

Key subtractions: F Julius Randle, C Naz Reid

Key retentions: G Ayo Dosunmu, G Bones Hyland, G Jaylen Clark

Wolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly continued to show his aggression, orchestrating a four-team trade with the Brooklyn Nets, Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets that sent out three-time All-Star Randle and the 2023-24 Sixth Man of the Year, Reid, and a future first-round pick to bring in the talented -- but polarizing -- Ball.

That move followed Connelly inking 6-foot-4 guard Dosunmu to a five-year, $112 million extension in June, following his acquisition at the deadline.

Minnesota also re-signed wing Clark and guard Hyland and acquired the 6-foot-6 Evans out of Duke with the No. 33 pick in the draft.

Coach Chris Finch also lost his top lieutenant on the bench, Micah Nori, who left to coach the Portland Trail Blazers. -- Dave McMenamin

Read the full Timberwolves offseason recap/season preview

Oklahoma City Thunder: Aug. 20
Key additions: C Aday Mara, G Bennett Stirtz

Key retentions: G Kenrich Williams, C Isaiah Hartenstein

Key subtractions: G Isaiah Joe, G Aaron Wiggins, G Luguentz Dort

The extensions for both Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren triggered in July, leading to a trio of financially motivated trades to slash the tax bill and cost-control the current roster.

They sent Isaiah Joe to Detroit and traded Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort to Atlanta in separate moves, eroding their depth.

General manager Sam Presti made clear in an interview with The Oklahoman that the impression he's been given from ownership is "the savings generated this summer, and from being out of the tax the last several years, will be re-allocated to future teams."

That would mean extra breathing room to eventually extend core young players such as Cason Wallace and Ajay Mitchell. Wallace, the likely replacement starter for Dort, is extension eligible off his rookie contract into October. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Thunder offseason recap/season preview

Denver Nuggets: Aug. 21
Key additions: Marvin Bagley III, Lonnie Walker IV

Key retentions: Spencer Jones, Tyus Jones

Key subtractions: Watson, Tim Hardaway Jr., Jonas Valanciunas

Finding a resolution to Watson's restricted free agency was Denver's most important piece of summer business.

Watson is a draft success story, rising from the 30th overall pick into one of the league's more intriguing young two-way wings. But retaining the 23-year-old would have been expensive -- via either a sky-high luxury tax bill or a salary-slashing move to get off an important veteran and generate more breathing room for a new deal.

After Wednesday's deal to send Watson to Cleveland, Denver's front office can shift its attention to escaping the salary cap's second apron. The Nuggets are currently the league's only team above it. -- Anthony Slater

Read the full Nuggets offseason recap/season preview

Southwest Division

Memphis Grizzlies: Aug. 14
Key additions: F Cameron Boozer, G D'Angelo Russell, F Isaiah Stewart, F Jerami Grant, F Kris Murray, C Quinten Post

Key retentions: None

Key subtractions: G Ja Morant, F Santi Aldama

Memphis finally traded Ja Morant, turning the last page from an ultimately disappointing chapter in franchise history, and already has his replacement as the face of the franchise in place: No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer. GM Zach Kleiman has overhauled the roster in the past few transaction cycles, acquiring four first-round picks when he traded Desmond Bane, a few more when he dealt Jaren Jackson Jr. and none for Morant, whose departure signaled a fresh start for the Grizzlies and him.

Memphis is in a full-blown youth movement, as 21-year-old forward GG Jackson is now the longest-tenured player on the roster. The Grizzlies say they believe they have a long-term foundation in place with their last few lottery picks: center Zach Edey, small forward Cedric Coward and power forward Boozer. -- Tim MacMahon

Read the full Grizzlies offseason recap/season preview

New Orleans Pelicans: Aug. 13
Key additions: None

Key retentions: C DeAndre Jordan

Key subtractions: F Kevon Looney

Despite capturing a combined 47 wins over the last two seasons under executive vice president Joe Dumars and general manager Troy Weaver, the Pelicans clearly believe that internal growth is the best path forward. Perhaps that justifies a near-silent summer in which the hiring of new coach Jamahl Mosley turned out to be the team's most notable move. Mosley becomes New Orleans' third coach since Dumars took the helm in April 2025. In addition to drafting Jaron Pierre Jr. in the second round, New Orleans signed just two new players over the summer in Kobe Bufkin and Hunter Dickinson, while bringing back 14 of the 15 players from last season's squad. -- Michael C. Wright

Read the full Pelicans offseason recap/season preview

Dallas Mavericks: Aug. 12
Key additions: F Morez Johnson Jr., F Zaccharie Risacher

Key retentions: Moussa Cisse

Key subtractions: Khris Middleton, Ryan Nembhard

The major changes made by the Mavericks this offseason were in the managerial and coaching ranks. After a seasonlong search, team governor Patrick Dumont hired Masai Ujiri to run the franchise's basketball operations, bringing the architect of the Toronto Raptors' 2019 title team to Dallas. Ujiri decided to part ways with coach Jason Kidd and recruited Dusty May, fresh off an NCAA title with Michigan, to replace him.

Johnson, who played for May at Michigan before the Mavs selected him with the No. 9 pick in the draft, is the headliner of the additions to the roster. Dallas added three potential immediate contributors in a six-team deal, acquiring former Grizzlies forward Santi Aldama, ex-Pistons guard Marcus Sasser and EuroLeague veteran Tarik Biberovic. The franchise also landed former No. 1 pick as part of the trade that sent Luguentz Dort from the Oklahoma City Thunder to the Atlanta Hawks. -- MacMahon

Read the full Mavericks offseason recap/season preview

Houston Rockets: Aug. 11
Key additions: G Marcus Smart, G Bogdan Bogdanovic

Key retentions: F Tari Eason

Key subtractions: F Dorian Finney-Smith, G Josh Okogie

After suffering a first-round postseason exit for the second consecutive season, the Rockets resisted the temptation to jump into the Giannis Antetokounmpo sweepstakes after adding former MVP Durant last summer. General manager Rafael Stone and coach Ime Udoka will instead lean on growth from the team's collection of young talent acquired in recent years, not to mention the continuity that comes with those players developing together over multiple seasons.

Houston signed Tari Eason to a five-year, $81.5 million extension over the summer. But outside of that, the Rockets focused on bolstering depth by bringing aboard veterans Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic. The club also brought in renowned shooting coach Chip Engelland from Oklahoma City. Engelland spent more than a decade with the San Antonio Spurs, winning two titles. -- Wright

Read the full Rockets offseason recap/season preview

San Antonio Spurs: Aug. 10
Key additions: F Tobias Harris

Key retentions: F Harrison Barnes

Key subtractions: None

San Antonio's surprising run to the NBA Finals never obscured its long-term vision for building a sustainable competitor around Victor Wembanyama. Clearly, the Frenchman views the future similarly, considering he signed a 25% max extension worth $252 million instead of the available 30% supermax escalators that would've rocketed the contract to $303 million.

Wembanyama did it to keep San Antonio's talented young core together for as long as possible, with added flexibility to acquire needed supporting players. The Spurs grabbed one of those in free agency in Harris, an experienced, reliable scorer who adds size (6-foot-8, 226 pounds) and physicality on defense while bolstering frontcourt depth in the draft. -- Wright

stories.headline: What makes Max Verstappen so good? Career, background and F1 records
stories.summary: Max Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and is facing 100 drivers in a unique event called Max vs. 100 where the Formula 1 star will attempt to overtake 100 challengers, starting from the back of the grid.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and is taking part in a unique event called Max vs 100 where the Formula 1 star will attempt to overtake 100 drivers, starting from the back of the grid.

The 28-year-old currently races in F1, the highest tier in motorsport. He is one of the fiercest competitors out there and is known for his aggressive driving style and fearless overtaking.

But if you have never heard of him, or want to learn more, here is everything you need to know.

- Max vs 100: F1 superstar Verstappen to race drivers in karting event - live on Disney+

Who is Max Verstappen?
Verstappen was born in Belgium to his Dutch father Jos and his Belgian mother Sophie. His father raced in F1 between 1994-2003 and had two podium finishes, while his mother competed in karts. He currently resides in Monaco.

Who does he race for?
Verstappen started racing go-karts when he was just four years old and started to compete in championships at seven.

He then made his way through the ranks winning several world and European titles in 2013. He raced just one season in Formula 3 before skipping Formula 2 and heading straight to Formula 1.

In 2015, he signed for Red Bull junior team Toro Rosso at the age of 17 before he was promoted to Red Bull a year later.

He then went on to become the youngest ever grand prix winner after taking victory at the Spanish Grand Prix and has been at Red Bull ever since, becoming the most successful driver at the team.

He signed a long-term contract back in March 2022 to stay at the Milton Keynes-based team until the end of 2028, and before the Dutch Grand Prix this year he penned a new deal keeping him at the team until 2030.

What has he achieved?
It was clear from the early days that Verstappen was going to be an exceptional racing driver and he's become a phenomenon since with a killer instinct.

He's had 244 race starts in F1 and has been on the top step of the podium 71 times. He's been on the podium 131 times and is just two pole positions away from reaching 50 career poles.

The Dutchman has four world championships which he won back-to-back in a dominant Red Bull era between 2021-2024.

He also has an impressive list of achievements to his name, one being in 2023 where he recorded the most wins [19] and the most podium finishes [21] in a single season. He also recorded 10 consecutive race victories.

When is Max vs 100?
The event is taking place on Sept. 16 and will be streamed live on Disney+.

Why is he racing in Max vs 100?

Verstappen has never been shy of getting his teeth stuck into other forms of motorsport away from Formula 1. He most recently made his debut at the iconic Nürburgring 24 Hours in May, driving a Mercedes-AMG GT3.

This will be a slightly different challenge for the Dutchman, but no doubt one he will enjoy with his competitive nature.

"In go-karts you learn all the basics: starts, defending, overtaking," Verstappen said. "Of course, I spent a long period of my life go-karting, so it's always nice to return."

The event is taking place at Silverstone in the U.K. and a circuit has been purpose-built for the occasion. It's set to be the biggest go-kart event in the world.

- Max Verstappen deal: Good news for Red Bull and F1, bad news for the driver market

- Max Verstappen ends F1 speculation by signing new Red Bull contract to 2030

How is his 2026 F1 season going?
The 2026 season is one with big regulation and rules changes and Red Bull are currently at the back of the front running teams, but are ahead of the midfield pack.

Verstappen is still searching for his first race win of the season, but has been on the podium four times.

He's currently sixth in the title championship and is 130 points adrift from title leader Kimi Antonelli.

stories.headline: Champions League schedule: Real Madrid open league phase vs. Inter Milan
stories.summary: Record 15-time European champions Real Madrid will start the league phase of the Champions League on Sept. 8 when they host Inter Milan.
stories.body:
Record 15-time European champions Real Madrid will start the league phase of the Champions League on Sept. 8 when they host coach José Mourinho's former club Inter Milan.

Match dates for each of the 36 teams' eight-game schedules were published Saturday by UEFA, two days after the draw in Monaco.

- Champions League draw: Good for Liverpool, bad for Barcelona

- Arsenal-Madrid, PSG-Barça highlight UCL draw

- Champions League draw becomes UEFA's latest stand against FIFA president Infantino

In two early starts on the opening day, Club Brugge will host Aston Villa and AEK Athens will welcome LASK, the newcomers from Austria. Both games will kick off at 6:45 p.m.

One day later, defending champions Paris Saint-Germain will host Slovan Bratislava -- coached by Yaya Touré, the first African leading a team at the league phase -- and Liverpool will host Atlético Madrid, a repeat of their opening game last season. That was a 3-2 win for Liverpool at Anfield.

Debut-making Sabah of Azerbaijan will start at Manchester United on Sept. 10, the same day Como host RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich welcome Bodo/Glimt.

Tough October for PSG
Manchester City hosting PSG on Oct. 14 is a highlight of the second round of games played more than one month later, after the new and extended four-game slate for national teams.

PSG will then face Barcelona at Parc des Princes on Oct. 20, one day before Bayern Munich host Arsenal.

Barcelona's next trip will then be a long way east to play Sabah in Baku on Nov. 25, before the Spanish champions hosts Man City on Dec. 8.

Arsenal will host Real Madrid on Dec. 9 for the first of coach Mourinho's scheduled two visits to London.

Madrid will return on the final match day, Jan. 27, to face Shakhtar Donetsk at Chelsea, where Mourinho won three Premier League titles for the club's Russian then-owner Roman Abramovich. Stamford Bridge is the Ukrainian champions' choice of neutral venue for its four home games.

Welcome to Norway
The two Norwegian teams each must have a home game in January, during their domestic offseason when the weather should be most severe, and both will be in the seventh round.

Bodo/Glimt will welcome Atlético Madrid to the Arctic Circle at their tiny stadium on Jan. 19 and Viking will host PSV Eindhoven in Stavanger one day later.

Final round
The final round on Jan. 27 sees all 18 games start at the same time, when it's 9 p.m. in central Europe, and Barcelona will host newcomers Como coached by their former star Cesc Fàbregas.

Como get the toughest January run-in after hosting PSG one week earlier.

PSG will finish by hosting Galatasaray, Arsenal will host Sabah and Bayern will host Real Betis.

The top eight teams in the final standings go directly to the round of 16 in March. Teams placed ninth to 24th enter the knockout playoffs in February to decide the other eight teams in the round of 16. Teams placed 25th to 36th are eliminated.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Song Yadong KO's Umar Nurmagomedov in massive UFC upset
stories.summary: Song Yadong pulled off a massive upset by knocking out heavily favored Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night in Shanghai.
stories.body:
Song Yadong saved the greatest performance of his career for his home country, knocking out former title challenger Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night on Saturday in Shanghai.

Song (24-9-1, 1 NC), a nearly 5-1 underdog at DraftKings Sportsbook, dropped Nurmagomedov with a short right hand, drawing a roar from the crowd when the fight was waved off at 1 minute, 48 seconds of Round 2.

"I believe in myself, and my team believed that I would win this fight," Song said through an interpreter. "They told me I would knock this guy out, and I did it."

It was the second straight fight in China for Song and his second straight win by finish. His most recent knockout win had been in 2023.

Song, making his first appearance in Shanghai since his UFC debut at age 19 in 2017, walked out to a hero's welcome.

"Nine years ago, I wanted to show I could walk in this Octagon," he said. "Nine years later, I want to prove I am the best in the world. I am the best Chinese fighter in the world."

The knockout came after Nurmagomedov (20-2) ducked out of the way of a left hand and right into the path of a short right hand, which connected near his right ear and sent him limply to the canvas. Song delivered three finishing shots on the mat before the referee jumped in.

That sent Song running around inside the cage in celebration, where he nearly ran into Nurmagomedov's younger brother and cornerman, PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, who had rushed in to check on his fallen brother. Usman Nurmagomedov appeared to throw an elbow in Song's direction as the elated winner was running past.

Song climbed atop the cage to soak in the fans' cheers before jumping down outside the cage and running into the crowd to get hugs and high-fives from fans.

"Maybe not today, maybe not tomorrow, maybe not next month, but I will be the first male Chinese UFC champion," Song said through the interpreter, with the "male" designation a nod to countrywoman Zhang Weili, a two-time women's champion at strawweight.

Song, who trains in Sacramento, California, switched to English and yelled, "Give me the title shot!"

stories.headline: Avalanche's Makar agrees to record deal worth $20.4M annually
stories.summary: Cale Makar has agreed to an eight-year extension with the Avalanche that will make him the highest-paid player in NHL history with a $20.4 million average annual value.
stories.body:
Cale Makar has agreed to an eight-year extension with the Colorado Avalanche that will make him the highest-paid player in NHL history.

The deal carries a $20.4 million average annual value. Makar is the first player in league history to make at least $20 million per season. The max a player could make, per percentage of the salary cap, is $20.8 million.

Makar, 27, has been a finalist for the Norris Trophy as the league's top defenseman for six consecutive seasons. He is one of only 14 players to win multiple Norris Trophies, winning the award twice -- most recently in 2025.

Makar was entering the final year of his contract, which carried a $9 million average annual value.

The deal carries a full no-movement clause, according to sources. The eight-year term carries significance because when the new collective bargaining rules kick in Sept. 15, players will be able to sign for a maximum of only seven years.

This summer has seen record-breaking contracts in the NHL thanks to a rising salary cap, including massive deals for young centers Macklin Celebrini and Leo Carlsson.

Makar is a centerpiece for the Avalanche, perennial Stanley Cup contenders who won the Presidents' Trophy last season.

stories.headline: Knights prop ruled out of NRL finals with mammoth ban
stories.summary: Jacob Saifiti's NRL season is all but over after the Newcastle prop was handed a four-game suspension for a high tackle on Warriors winger Luke Laulilii.
stories.body:
Jacob Saifiti's NRL season is all but over after the Newcastle prop was handed a four-game suspension for a high tackle on Warriors winger Luke Laulilii.

Saifiti was sent off in the first half of Sunday's 46-32 defeat in Auckland and was handed a grade two reckless high tackle charge by the NRL's match review committee on Monday morning.

The Knights are on the bye for the final round of the regular season, meaning Saifiti's ban will only kick in for their first finals game.

Newcastle - currently sitting seventh - will play an elimination final in week one but even if they were to upset the odds and qualify for the grand final, the Fijian prop would still be on the sidelines with suspension.

Saifiti's only hope of playing in the NRL again this season hinge on the prop contesting the charge at the judiciary on Tuesday in a bid to reduce his punishment.

Should the front-rower fight the suspension and lose his appeal, he will have another week added to his four-game ban.

Elsewhere, Cronulla prop Tom Hazelton is set to miss Cronulla's final regular season game against Melbourne after being cited for a hip-drop tackle on Ronald Volkman.

Hazelton was sin-binned by referee Ashley Klein late in Sunday's loss to Parramatta but will serve a one-game ban with an early guilty plea and be free to return for week one of the final series.

stories.headline: Summer transfer window: Grading big signings in men's soccer
stories.summary: The 2026 summer transfer window is open. Here is how we rated the biggest deals.
stories.body:
Premier League clubs spent a record £3 billion ($4 billion) in a 2025 summer transfer window that finished with a bang thanks to Liverpool's £125 million ($169 million) signing of Newcastle United striker Alexander Isak. But with a FIFA World Cup in the middle of the window in 2026, will things stay the same?

The window opened on June 15 for the Premier League and July 1 for most of the other major European leagues.

Here are grades for all the major confirmed transfers in the men's game, with each listed by date and then by highest fee.

All fees are reported unless confirmed with an asterisk.

Aug. 31

Allan Elias

€37.5M (£32M; $43.7M)
Palmeiras: B

Manchester City: A-

Allan Elias is one of Brazil's most exciting talents, and at just 22 years of age, had already become the leading light in a strong Palmeiras team. They'll miss him badly, but a deal potentially worth €40 million makes him their third-most-expensive departure in history, behind only Endrick (Real Madrid) and Estêvão (Chelsea). It was too good to refuse.

He joins Man City as part of a sizable refresh, nominally taking Savio's spot in the squad as a depth winger, but he's capable of playing across the forward line and even as a central midfielder or wingback too.

Aug. 30

Ollie Watkins

£51M ($69M)
Aston Villa: A-

Al Hilal: B

Last season, Watkins became the 12th player in history to score 100 goals for Aston Villa and led the attacking line as they won the Europa League. He should be a hero, but instead left under a cloud, as he reportedly refused to play on the opening day of the Premier League while pushing for an exit -- despite Villa not having another fit striker.

It's an emotional departure for Villa, but in the cold light of day, £51 million-plus add-ons for a player who turns 31 in December is excellent business. Al Hilal, meanwhile, get the proven goal scorer they've been after all summer.

Rafael Leão

€45M ($52M)
AC Milan: B

Galatasaray: B

Gala fought hard to secure the signature of Leão, outbidding Aston Villa en route to landing the 27-year-old. It's yet another marquee transfer following last summer's additions of Victor Osimhen and Leroy Sané, though while sources told ESPN the total fee was €45 million, the Turkish club claimed publicly it was €38 million.

It's not the ending AC Milan would have envisioned, as the Portugal international was once regarded as one of the best wingers on the planet and his transfer valued at €175 million -- but at 27, having lost his way a little, it's the one they must accept. The fee is reasonable and it's a big salary off the books, which is crucial following the Rossoneri's own spending of over €120 million to bring in Gonçalo Ramos and Diego Moreira.

Emiliano Martínez

£7.5M ($10M)
Aston Villa: C+

Chelsea: A

Martínez might go down as Villa's greatest goalkeeper, but his time at the club had come to a natural end. He expressed a desire to leave, his massive weekly wages were difficult to justify given the financial pressures on the club, and his replacement, Zion Suzuki, is already in place.

Chelsea have picked up one of the best goalkeepers in the world for a small fee. He'll turn 34 in September so it's not a long-term solution, but it will make them a lot better immediately, which is what's required after last season's 10th-place finish.

Aug. 28

Nicolas Jackson

£47.5M ($65M)
Chelsea: B

Aston Villa: A-

Jackson and Unai Emery finally reunite. The two worked together brilliantly at Villarreal in 2022, so when the time came for Villa to find a striker to replace Ollie Watkins, this was the obvious place to turn. At 25, and after a failed loan at Bayern Munich last season, the Senegal international is ready to be the main man in a Premier League forward line.

Villa will be delighted with the initial £47.5 million fee, which is cheap for a player of Jackson's quality. But a further £17.5 million worth of potential add-ons will mean Chelsea are happy enough too, as there's scope for this deal to reach the £65 million point they always wanted.

Aug. 27

Liam Delap

£45M ($61M)
Chelsea: A+

Nottingham Forest: B-

Delap joined Chelsea for £30 million last summer, failed to impress, and now moves on in a deal that could rise to £50 million with add-ons. It's a financial masterclass from the Blues, who correctly bet that even if things didn't work out for him at Stamford Bridge, there would be plenty of suitors for him a year on.

Forest's direct style of play will suit Delap, who likes to receive longer passes, run the channels and jockey with defenders in space. In short, he'll probably look like he did for Ipswich Town in 2024-25, for whom he scored 12 league goals despite the campaign ending in relegation.

Omar Marmoush

Loan
Manchester City: A-

Tottenham: B

Marmoush was brought to City from Frankfurt for around £60 million during a panicked January 2025 transfer window. There were occasions where he flashed brilliance, but ultimately he was never able to fully settle into the team. Presented with the opportunity to make their money back on the deal, with the Egyptian now 27, it's no wonder City said yes.

It could prove a savvy deal for Spurs, though. Marmoush is technically strong and comes alive in the box, so should feel comfortable playing in Roberto De Zerbi's forward line. This is certainly one of the better value deals the club have struck this summer, as the loan has a £50 million obligation to sign him next year.

Leon Goretzka

Free
Bayern Munich: B

Aston Villa: B

Goretzka's eight-year spell at Bayern Munich was hugely successful and laden with trophies. Now 31, he is not the elite, box-to-box midfielder he was back in 2020, but he can still play to a high level, score goals and provide an experienced head in the dressing room.

After a summer of incredible upheaval, the German is exactly the kind of presence Aston Villa could use. He should provide cover in central midfield for Amadou Onana, who tore his ACL with Belgium at the World Cup, as well as impact higher up the pitch if needed.

Aug. 26

Ayyoub Bouaddi

€95M ($110M)
Lille: A

Manchester City: B

Over the last two years, Bouaddi has marked himself out as one of -- if not the -- most impressive young midfield talents in the game. He's just 18 years old, yet has already played 96 games for Lille in all competitions, excelling against the likes of Real Madrid and PSG, and he waltzed into the World Cup completely unphased to dominate for Morocco.

Both Lille and City will rightly feel like they've struck good deals here. For the former, €95 million (plus another €5 million in add-ons) is a transformative amount of money, especially with the state of France's broadcast revenues; for the latter, they've nipped in early to sign a player that could go on to become one of the best in the world.

Nico González

£48M ($65M)
Manchester City: A

Newcastle United: B

Nico's time at Man City felt downright bizarre. After signing on deadline day for £50 million in February 2025, he fluctuated from a key central midfielder under Pep Guardiola to being completely left out in the cold. Clearly, new boss Enzo Maresca isn't convinced either, so he's allowed him to move on for £48 million with £4 million in add-ons -- which means they got their money back, essentially.

For Newcastle, this is a really smart pickup in a market that has seen some central midfielders move for wild transfer fees. The Spaniard did enough in his 59 appearances for City to prove he's a very good player who can immediately upgrade the Magpies' setup.

Aug. 25

Savio

£75M ($102M)
Manchester City: A+

Tottenham: D

This is a jaw-dropping deal ... and not in a good way for Spurs. Spending a fee of £75 million, which could rise to £85 million with bonuses, to sign a player who has scored two Premier League goals in two seasons, is astonishing. There's no doubt Savio [formerly known as Savinho] is a good player, and at 22 has youth on his side, but this feels beyond excessive even in this market.

City, naturally, will be delighted to receive such a huge amount for a player whose transfer cost them just £30 million two summers ago, who did not perform to the expected level, and who was not part of the plan moving forward under Enzo Maresca.

Carlos Baleba

£65M ($88.7M)
Brighton & Hove Albion: B-

Manchester United: B+

United finally have their man. They've been tracking Baleba for well over a year and tried to sign him last summer only to be quoted a fee of £100 million. But after a tough year for the midfielder, where his stock fell, the Red Devils have agreed a substantially cheaper deal of £65 million, plus another £5 million in add-ons.

Based on last season's performances, Brighton won't really miss him. But based on the season before, when the Cameroon international dominated Premier League midfields, they will. If United can restore him to those levels, they've bagged a bargain.

Aug. 21

Curtis Jones

€35M (£30M; $41M)
Liverpool: C+

Inter Milan: A

Inter's supermarket sweep of talented, yet somehow undervalued English talent continues as Jones follows Djed Spence and John Stones through the door. The 25-year-old is a superb midfielder who is extremely comfortable dictating possession and can play in a variety of roles.

For Liverpool it's a minor disaster to lose such a player -- an academy product good enough to play a major role for the club -- and for such a modest fee.

Ezri Konsa

£51M (€59M; $70M)
Aston Villa: C+

Arsenal: B

Arsenal clearly sense an opportunity to register back-to-back Premier League title wins and won't let William Saliba's back injury jeopardize that. In Konsa, they've signed a plug-and-play, top-tier center back who can also cover the right side -- which is seemingly Mikel Arteta's favourite type of player.

But this really stings for Villa, who have lost a defensive stalwart and a model of consistency for seven years in their back line. They offered him a new contract to try to tempt him to stay, but he'll turn 29 in October and felt this was his chance at a big move. A fee of £51 million plus £4 million in add-ons is an OK fee on paper, but it's probably not enough to replace his quality like for like.

Aug. 20

João Cancelo

Free
Al Hilal: D

Barcelona: A

Al Hilal spent €25 million to land Cancelo from Manchester City in 2024, but it feels like they got very little value out of the deal. A total of 22 league appearances in his first season was OK, but he made just two the following year before being loaned to Barcelona; now the Portugal international has terminated his contract in Saudi Arabia in order to join the Blaugrana permanently.

This is obviously ideal for Barça, who are working to a budget but have several holes in the squad to fill. Even at 32, Cancelo is a quality player who can execute Hansi Flick's system and cover both full back positions.

Aug. 19

Tijjani Reijnders

€61M (£52M; $71M)
Manchester City: A

Al Qadsiah: B

A €55 million signing from AC Milan last summer, Reijnders made a bright start for the club, bringing real excitement around his arrival. But he quickly tailed off, and now the new manager Enzo Maresca has clearly deemed him surplus to requirements as he rebuilds City's midfield.

Given that this is a transfer that effectively failed from City's point of view, they've done brilliantly to make a profit on his departure. He should quickly become a key figure at Al Qadsiah given his talent.

Diego Moreira

€50M ($58M)
Strasbourg: A

AC Milan: C+

Moreira joined Strasbourg in 2024 after a year with sister-club Chelsea and really blossomed. He's a tricky, quick winger who is always pirouetting and backheeling away from tackles, but has also taken in some experience as a wing back. That positional versatility will serve him extremely well under manager Rúben Amorim.

But it should be noted that Moreira is still developing; at 22, he has some rough edges that need to be cleaned up, and this is no small fee (plus €16 million or so in add-ons) to operate under. Strasbourg, meanwhile, will be delighted with the quick flip.

Zion Suzuki

€30M (£26M; $35M)

Real Madrid: A-

When Chelsea's ownership group drew up their transfer strategy, this is surely not what it was supposed to look like. Cucurella is one of the few signings that has unequivocally succeeded, yet here they are losing him for a fairly modest fee, potentially rising to €60M with add-ons.

The Blues' loss is Madrid's gain: Barcelona academy graduate Cucurella returns to Spain as a fully fledged international and trophy winner, shoring up the left-back area in Madrid nicely. José Mourinho will love his blood-and-thunder style.

Ismael Saibari

€55M ($64M)
PSV Eindhoven: A

Bayern Munich: B

Saibari has blossomed over the last two years, contributing 52 goals and assists for PSV in the Champions League and Eredivisie play and securing his place as Morocco's first-choice striker. He scored at the 2026 World Cup to further enhance his reputation.

Bayern will appreciate those scoring numbers, but they will also love his ability to drop deep, receive the ball and create. It's what Harry Kane already does for them to a world class level, and now Bayern have found a very capable backup. It's a good stylistic fit for the German giants, while for PSV, it's a club record departure.

Piero Hincapié

€40M (£34.5M; $46M)
Bayer Leverkusen: C

Arsenal: A

Hincapié's loan to Arsenal has become a permanent move after certain conditions were met. He proved an excellent pickup last summer, ably sharing the left-back role with Riccardo Calafiori and covering at center back too.

Factoring in the initial loan fee of €6 million, this looks to have cost the Gunners just shy of €50 million all in. For a player of this established quality and age (24), it goes down as an absolute bargain.

Emmanuel Emegha

€25M (£22M; $29M)
Strasbourg: B

Chelsea: B

Chelsea struck a deal to sign Emegha in the summer of 2025, but opted to let him stay at sister club Strasbourg and continue developing for another year. It was a good idea, but things didn't go to plan as the Dutchman missed most of last season due to injury.

For a player who stands at 6-foot-5, he is extremely fast, with great movement, but he is unreliable in front of goal and underperformed his xG by three in 2024-25. Emegha has huge potential and is still only 23, but he probably isn't ready to start for Chelsea just yet.

Robert Lewandowski

Free transfer
Barcelona: B

Chicago Fire FC: B+

The Chicago Fire won the race to sign legendary striker Lewandowski, who may be into his late 30s but still scored 14 goals from 17 starts in LaLiga last season. He'll join MLS top scorer Hugo Cuypers (13 goals this term) in what is now a fearsome front two on paper.

It was certainly time for him to depart Barcelona, where he excelled since joining in 2022, but also accounted for a huge portion of the wage bill at a club that's been right up against it financially for some time.

Bernardo Silva

Free
Manchester City: D

Real Madrid: A

Silva, who is one of the most tactically versatile and intelligent players the sport has ever seen, was linked strongly to each of Spain's big three clubs. But Los Blancos will benefit hugely from his presence in a variety of ways.

After nine incredible years at City, there was little need for the club to recoup any sort of fee for him, but this one still really hurts. The Portugal midfielder was a crucial component of the team and the dressing room and a symbol of the Pep Guardiola era.

Ibrahima Konaté

Free
Liverpool: D

Real Madrid: B-

Konaté's athleticism is off the charts, and when he's in good form, he's close to unbeatable at the back. But inconsistency has long troubled his game, and reports in Spain suggest not only has he earned a huge signing bonus of €20 million, but he's more than tripled his weekly wage with this move.

From Madrid's perspective, this is no free transfer. But from Liverpool's perspective it is. They get absolutely nothing in return for a very good player, but have at least covered themselves for this eventuality with new €70 million arrival Jérémy Jacquet (agreed in January).

Antoine Griezmann

Free
Atletico Madrid: B

Orlando City: A

Griezmann's long farewell to Atlético was a tearjerker, and it feels right that the 35-year-old forward opted for a new challenge, on a different continent, rather than moved to another European club. He was a great servant to the club for a long time, negating the need to receive any kind of fee for him.

Orlando have had a poor campaign to date and could use all the help they can get; Griezmann's quality and personality is a great start to turning things around.

June 30

Gonçalo Ramos

€74M ($84M)
PSG: A

AC Milan: C+

First, Milan appointed former Manchester United manager Rúben Amorim as coach. Then they handed him his first new weapon: Ramos, a Champions League winner and a potent goal scorer -- albeit via a bit-part role with PSG these past three years.

This is a gargantuan outlay from the Italian giants, who have smashed their transfer record by more than €20 million for a player who has too often found himself kicking his heels for club and country of late. PSG, meanwhile, have banked €74 million, potentially rising to around €80 million, for a squad player; they'll rightly be delighted with that.

Alejandro Grimaldo

€20M ($22.7M)
Bayer Leverkusen: C

Atlético Madrid: A

Grimaldo will finally play in Spain's top tier, having left Barcelona's academy in 2016 without a first-team appearance to his name. He's blossomed abroad, at both Benfica and Bayer Leverkusen, developing into one of the best attacking fullbacks in the game. At €20 million, this is a steal for Atleti -- even if he is 30 years old.

Leverkusen don't stand a chance of replacing his quality like-for-like with a humble fee, and they've reluctantly said goodbye to one of their best players during that famous unbeaten title run in 2023-24.

June 18

Jan Paul van Hecke

£52M ($70M)
Brighton & Hove Albion: B+

Tottenham: B

Van Hecke has slowly developed into one of the Premier League's best center backs. The Netherlands international has long been one of the best passers and dribblers from the back, and now he's become a sturdier, meaner defender, too.

At 25, he's ready for the next step, and reuniting with manager Roberto De Zerbi at Tottenham feels like a brilliant match. Brighton were resigned to losing him given he had just one year left on his contract and did well to hold out for a fee above £50 million.

Víctor Muñoz

€40M (£35M; $46M)
Osasuna: B+

Liverpool: B-

Muñoz is an incredibly busy, buzzing winger who tears around the pitch, tries to beat defenders one-on-one and shoots willingly. Stylistically that makes him a good fit for Andoni Iraola, but Liverpool are gambling slightly on the 23-year-old stepping up to the elite level quickly.

For Osasuna, this is a record departure -- but not quite the huge payday it looks like. They only hold 50% of the player's rights, with Real Madrid holding the other half; that means half €40M fee will go to Los Blancos.

June 15

Marcos Senesi

Free
Bournemouth: D

Tottenham: A

Senesi was one of the outstanding center backs in the Premier League last season. A committed defender, a physical presence and a brilliant passer from the back, he stood out as one of the best free agents heading into the summer, and Spurs have won the race for his signature.

His signing does raise some questions for the club to answer. Will captain Cristian Romero be departing? Is the plan to play with two left-footers (Senesi and Micky van de Ven), or will it be a back three? Though none of that detracts from the fact this deal is a coup.

Andy Robertson

Free
Liverpool: B

Tottenham: B

Tottenham came close to signing Robertson in January and have now finally sealed the deal. The 32-year-old defender's time at Liverpool had come to a natural end as he passed his peak and Milos Kerkez replaced him in the XI.

Roberto De Zerbi will value the Scotland international's passing ability and the Spurs squad badly need his leadership qualities -- although they have reportedly paid a premium in wages for a player who won't necessarily be first choice.

June 29

Rasmus Højlund

€44M (£38M; $51M)
Manchester United: B+

Napoli: B+

Højlund's loan to Napoli was made permanent the moment the Italian giants qualified for the Champions League. The Denmark striker led the attacking line all season long, contributing 16 goals in total, and rebounded well from his disappointing spell at Man United.

It's a good deal for both clubs, as €44 million (plus a €6 million loan fee last season) for a reliable goal scorer represents strong value for Napoli, while United will be pleased to make a fair chunk of their money back on a signing that cost them an initial €75 million and simply did not work out.

stories.headline: Shepard has 22nd double-double this season, Wings beat Sun 97-71
stories.summary: — Arike Ogunbowale scored 18 points, Jessica Shepard had 17 points and 10 rebounds, and the Dallas Wings beat the Connecticut Sun 97-71 on Sunday night in the final game before the FIBA World Cup break.
stories.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- — Arike Ogunbowale scored 18 points, Jessica Shepard had 17 points and 10 rebounds, and the Dallas Wings beat the Connecticut Sun 97-71 on Sunday night in the final game before the FIBA World Cup break.


The Wings (24-16) have won four in a row and have their most wins in a season since 2007, when the franchise also won 24 games as the Detroit Shock. The Shock won a franchise-record 25 games in 2003 on their way to the first of three WNBA championships.


Dallas moved into a three-way tie with New York and Washington for sixth in the WNBA standings, two games back of Indiana and Atlanta.


Shepard had her 22nd double-double this season, second most in the WNBA — after Angel Reese with 29 — to extend the franchise record. Paige Bueckers added 15 points and six assists and Maddy Siegrist scored 11 for Dallas.


Aaliyah Edwards scored 21 of her career-best tying 26 points in the first half for the Sun (10-30). Charlisse Leger-Walker hit five 3-pointers and finished with 17 points.


Saniya Rivers made a driving layup that gave the Sun their first lead about 4 1/2 minutes into the game at 11-10, but Bueckers scored inside 11 seconds later to put Dallas back in front for good.


Connecticut, which trailed by 13 at halftime, made 4 of 17 (23.5%) from the field, 1 of 6 from behind the arc, and hit 3 of 6 from the free-throw line as it was outscored 23-12 in the third quarter.


Up next
Sun: Plays Sept. 17 at Atlanta.


Wings: Host Los Angeles on Sept. 17.

This story has been updated to correct that the Shock won 24 games in 2007, not 24 straight.

stories.headline: Caleb Wilson and a new regime: The summer that changed the Chicago Bulls
stories.summary: It has been an offseason of change in Chicago. Now, No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson and a new Bulls front office have turned the tide for a franchise lost in the middle.
stories.body:
IT'S AUG. 22 and Chicago Bulls fans pack the area surrounding the United Center. The team is hosting its annual two-day fan festival, Bulls fest, and fans are lining up for the chance to meet the 20-year-old who has not only provided a new, unfamiliar hope around the franchise this summer but someone to pull the franchise out of a decade of irrelevance. This is Caleb Wilson's introduction to Chicago.

The lines for his meet-and-greet wrap around the atrium. The next event of the fest is a slam dunk contest in the parking lot, where Wilson is one of the judges. But first, he screams and sticks his tongue out for a hype video in front of a crowd of fans standing in front of the Michael Jordan statue.

The image -- a juxtaposition from where the franchise once was and where it now plans to go -- is impossible to ignore.

The anticipation has been growing for months, ever since the Bulls selected the North Carolina star No. 4 overall during the NBA draft in June.

The Bulls hope Wilson is the new face of the franchise, a much-needed refresh for a team that has missed the playoffs in eight of the past nine seasons.

The hype began to boil after Wilson's electric showing during his first in-game action at the Las Vegas summer league. Wilson finished his first professional game with 35 points, the second-highest total for a rookie debut in summer league history, and knocked down seven 3-pointers in the process.

In his second game, Wilson soared over 6-foot-11 Jazz center Jonas Aidoo to throw down an emphatic dunk in one of the top highlight-reel plays of the summer.

By his fourth and final game, Hall of Fame forward Kevin Garnett sat courtside to get a glimpse of the rookie to whom he started to draw comparisons. Both are 6-foot-10, wiry 215-pound players buoyed by elite athleticism. "I actually think his floor is Kevin Garnett," Warriors forward Draymond Green said on his podcast this summer.

"And man, if that's your floor, oh my god. Do you know how great KG was? I actually think with Caleb Wilson, Kevin Garnett could be his floor. That's how special I think Caleb Wilson is."

Teams are normally hesitant to make grand proclamations from summer league, but Wilson's performance stood out.

"He looks," one team source told ESPN, "like we got a dude."

The Bulls believe Wilson is yet another new pillar of an almost entirely new leadership structure. They hired a new head of basketball operations, Bryson Graham, who had a reputation for building through the draft and finding young talent.

Graham then selected a new head coach, Tiago Splitter, who has a background of player development success stories. They selected Wilson and then rounded out the roster with veterans such as Norman Powell and Nic Claxton, but Wilson's development will be the franchise's top priority in the 2026-27 season.

"We just want to see internal growth from our young guys and even from our veteran players," Graham told ESPN. "We just want to see a team that's going to go out there, represent this city well, play hard and obviously continue to grow and continue to develop."

Though expectations are high for Wilson across the league, team sources said there is no pressure for the Bulls to compete for a play-in or playoff spot in a loaded Eastern Conference. After years of the Bulls trying to jump-start themselves back into relevance, the decision-makers in Chicago are preaching patience before a resurrection.

For his part, though, Wilson has made his goals for his rookie season clear.

"I expect to have Rookie of the Year, honestly," Wilson said. "I'm going to work hard. I'm going to do what it takes. I feel like the team is really good for me and how I envision to play."

THE SUMMER LEAGUE debut was eye-popping in a smaller, but even more tantalizing, way.

Wilson's seven made 3s were more than he made during his entire freshman season at North Carolina.

Concerns about his shooting ability -- along with an injury that shortened his college season and kept him out of the NCAA tournament -- were the biggest knocks against him entering the draft and why he was ultimately selected behind AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson and Cameron Boozer in the 2026 draft class.

To explain and perhaps ease those concerns, Wilson pointed to the system at North Carolina, one that did not ask him to take 3-pointers (he averaged 1.1 attempts per game), but he also noted how he began working to improve his shot once the college season ended.

"I'm glad I didn't shoot 3s in college," Wilson said after a practice this summer. "Because if I did, I wouldn't be here. I don't know where I'd be. I don't think I'd be a Bull."

A broken thumb and left wrist fracture ended Wilson's college season in February, and he couldn't move his thumb while wearing a cast that kept the digit straight. But he could still hold a ball to practice his form, and he did so -- over and over, all summer.

Wilson estimates he has been shooting between 2,000 and 2,500 3-pointers per day.

For as much as Wilson's performance on the court generated buzz throughout the league, his work ethic has only heightened the excitement inside the organization.

He cried before his professional debut, five months to the day since the end of his college season, because he said he had been waiting for that moment for so long. The other top picks in his class were shut down from action after two or three summer league games, but Wilson pushed to keep playing, texting Graham to ask to play on the second night of a back-to-back in Chicago's third game of the summer.

Wilson averaged 23.5 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 2.5 blocks in four summer league games at and was named to the all-summer league first team. When informed that his 35-point debut was one of the highest-scoring debut performances in the history of the event, Wilson shrugged it off because his team lost.

Outside of his time in Las Vegas, Wilson has been a mainstay in Chicago since the draft. He works out at the team's practice facility in the morning and then returns around 8 or 9 p.m., along with fellow first-round pick Dailyn Swain, who was selected No. 15 by Chicago in June, for workouts that routinely approach midnight.

"Everybody highlights his athleticism, which is generational," Swain said. "But he can do a lot of things. He's really good facing up at the elbow, jab. He has a really good midrange shot. He's been knocking down 3s, so he's widening his arsenal."

GRAHAM'S FIRST MAJOR hire as the team's head of basketball operations was to bring in Splitter, a coach whose vision Graham touted as close to his own.

As an interim coach last season, Splitter led the Portland Trail Blazers to a surprise playoff appearance as the No. 7 seed in the Western Conference, but during his introductory news conference in Chicago, neither Splitter nor Graham focused on repeating such an unlikely jump.

Graham touted Splitter's player development credentials, from helping Deni Avdija become an All-Star in Portland to his days as an assistant coach, guiding Jarrett Allen as a member of the Brooklyn Nets' player development staff in 2019 or a young Alperen Sengun as an assistant with the Houston Rockets in 2023.

"The first thing you do is connect," Splitter said. "That's the foundation of everything you do, especially at this level. If you don't have that, it's really hard to demand and make them respect you. The foundation is [to] connect with the players in different ways."

Splitter started his bond with Wilson early this summer. It began with a shared interest in music and with Splitter being surprised at Wilson's range in music tastes. The 19-year-old began learning the guitar in his spare time this summer and has played everything from hip-hop to classical to country.

"Very interesting young guy," Splitter said. "You see how his brain functions and the variety of things he can have a conversation about."

Splitter also stepped in to coach the Bulls at summer league for the team's first two games in Las Vegas. He said he wanted the opportunity to establish a culture with his young players. For a young coach still finding his identity, it was good practice for the challenge of taking over a franchise starved for a winner with newfound expectations of the future.

"He's really detailed," Wilson said. "He knows what he wants you to do and he's pretty serious. Most coaches, you have coaches that are joking around and stuff like that. Tiago's pretty serious and he knows what he wants.

"I'd rather have someone who's serious and straightforward with me, so I know what I can do better."

Wilson functioned as the team's point guard and primary ball handler for most of the summer -- something that wasn't featured in Garnett's Hall of Fame career -- but those duties will lessen by the start of the season when he's surrounded by Josh Giddey, Powell and third-year forward Matas Buzelis, who will help run the offense after starting 77 games last season.

"It builds a healthy environment," Graham said. "It gives the younger guys confidence, too, because they know that, when it is going bad, they have some guys that have done it, some guys that have won and had success and they can learn. It's just really important for the overall development of our younger players and the health of our team."

In his previous experiences as a head coach, Splitter has been malleable in his style of play.

He coached in France and led Paris Basketball, a club in the first division of French basketball, to the EuroLeague playoffs with a fast-paced offense.

With the Blazers a season ago, defense became the calling card. Chicago represents his first chance to shape a young roster in his own image.

"You have to adapt your system to the players you have," Splitter said.

"Yes, I have a vision. I have a certain way I want to play, but you also have to explore what they do best. That's what we're going to do here."

It's what Splitter was hired to accomplish -- to help nurture and guide Chicago's roster while its young players develop.

In what has become an annual tradition, Bulls players convened in Miami last week for a player-run minicamp a few weeks before training camp.

And as the hype for Wilson continues to rise, the Bulls rookie remains focused on his ultimate goal.

"I do expect to win," he said. "Whatever it takes to win is what I'm going to do."

stories.headline: Concussion saga not a distraction for finals-bound Cats
stories.summary: Geelong players are adamant the AFL club's concussion saga hasn't been a distraction as the Cats gear up for finals while relishing Jake Kolodjashnij's return to the fold.
stories.body:
Geelong players are adamant the AFL club's concussion saga hasn't been a distraction as the Cats gear up for finals while relishing Jake Kolodjashnij's return to the fold.

The Cats were last week fined $140,000 for failing to officially let the AFL know about the concussion waiver in Kolodjashnij's contract.

The penalty is $100,000 plus a suspended sanction of $40,000, which stems from the league fining Geelong last October after an investigation into the club's third-party agreements.

Kolodjashnij, who came forward as the player involved shortly after the story broke and has not played at any level since, returned to the club last week ahead of the finals.

When asked about Kolodjashnij's return, midfielder Tom Atkins, the defender's 2022 premiership teammate, said: "Awesome. Kola's one of my favourite teammates, so yeah, to see him back, feeling a bit better.

"Obviously we'd love him to be back playing and back in training, but hopefully that can get itself sorted soon.

"But just having him in the rooms and seeing him smiling again is good."

Asked on Monday whether he or another player had a discussion around a similar concussion agreement, Atkins said: "No".

The experienced midfielder indicated the concussion saga, and last week's handing down of a fine, hadn't been discussed with the players.

"No, it's very much been, our focus has been performing on the weekends, and yeah, we just wanted to make sure Kola was alright as teammates and as friends," Atkins said.

"That's probably the extent of the detail that we looked into it as players. So yeah, just care for Kola, that's pretty much it."

Geelong start their September campaign in Friday night's blockbuster elimination final against Carlton at the MCG.

Asked whether the concussion saga had been a distraction, Atkins said: "not at all.

"Each individual's different, but I think Jake himself - that's the last thing he'd want - to distract from our performance.

"And I think it's a good quality of our playing group is we're mature and we're able to compartmentalise a bit.

"So we can show care for Jake during the week, but we can also put that to the side and perform on the weekend. I think we've done that."

stories.headline: Lando Norris signs new contract to stay at McLaren until at least 2030
stories.summary: Reigning world champion Lando Norris has committed his long-term future to McLaren after signing a new contract to remain at the team until at least 2030.
stories.body:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris has committed his long-term future to McLaren after signing a new contract to remain at the team until at least 2030.

The deal, which includes one of his title-winning Formula 1 cars as a gift from the team, also has the option of a "multiyear" extension beyond 2030.

Norris, 26, who made his F1 debut with McLaren in 2019, last signed a multiyear contract extension in 2024 that was believed to run until 2027.

Norris' future at McLaren had not looked in doubt and was only cemented by his championship-winning season in 2025, which made him the first driver since Lewis Hamilton in 2008 to win F1's top prize with the team.

The new contract represents a trend in long-term commitments between star drivers and teams in this year's driver market after Max Verstappen committed to Red Bull until 2030 last week and Charles Leclerc signed a new multiyear deal with Ferrari earlier this season.

"McLaren is my home, and I'm very pleased to be signing a new contract to keep me with the team until at least 2030," Norris said. "When I started this journey nine years ago, I was clear about the goals I wanted to achieve: to get McLaren back to the front and to win Championships.

"We've achieved that goal, but we want more, we want to keep on winning, and we know as a team that we're capable of achieving it. I can't wait to get back in the car in Monza and I'm very excited about what the future holds for us, both over the rest of this season, and in the coming years."
